sentence: This project studies how calcium signaling inside cilia helps set the position of the heart and other organs during development.
This project studies how adeno-associated viral vectors set up their epigenetic state in different cells and species, to help choose vectors for human gene therapy.
This project uses a microbe called Listeria seeligeri to study how four kinds of CRISPR immune systems defend against viruses and how viruses block them.
This project studies how two signaling pathways control the specification and patterning of photoreceptor neurons in the retina.
This project builds artificial intelligence methods and software that predict health outcomes linked to substance abuse in patients with HIV infection.
This project combines implementation science with epidemiology to help control zoonotic disease threats through a One Health framework.
This project tests an intervention to promote patient-centered communication in ovarian cancer care and whether natural language processing can analyze clinic visit transcripts.
This project studies how a gene linked to Catel-Manzke Syndrome guides craniofacial development and what happens when it is disrupted.
This project provides services for studies on gene sequence and function, including bioinformatics analysis and checking gene expression at the protein level.
This project tries to find out which epigenetic factors and mechanisms contribute to cancer risk, initiation, progression and treatment resistance.
This project tests whether pulsed electric fields, together with immunotherapies, can destroy solid tumors and trigger an immune response against them.
This project studies how stress changes the makeup of ribosomes in neurons through ribosomal protein genes and ribosomal protein pseudogenes.
This project uses genetically diverse mice and parasite strains to find out why some hosts are susceptible to the parasite Toxoplasma gondii.
This project studies how a protein regulates assembly in skeletal muscles and how this affects muscle bioenergetics.
This project tests a genomic surveillance approach that detects selection in parasite genes over time to give early warning of artemisinin resistance in Africa.
This project provides mass spectrometry services for studying proteins, metabolites and lipids to support cancer research.
This project develops statistical and machine learning methods and software to analyze large genetic and genomic data in cancer research.
This project improves a sensor with two nanopores that identifies single molecules, by upgrading the devices, the hardware and the machine learning models.
This project studies how ethanol changes the amount of the protein Prohibitin 1 and whether this can protect against colorectal liver metastasis.
